plan.title: How Do Volcanoes Erupt? A Video for Kids
plan.description: A gentle explainer for six-year-olds about how hot melted rock called magma rises and makes a volcano erupt. Learn why some volcanoes explode and others flow slowly.

beats.narration: Did you know the ground under your feet has a secret? Deep down, it is so hot that rock melts! Can you guess what happens next?
Deep inside the Earth, some rock gets so hot that it melts into a thick, glowing goo. This hot goo is called magma.

props.definition: Hot, melted rock found deep inside the Earth.
props.example: Magma is hiding under a volcano.

beats.narration: A volcano is an opening in the Earth's surface. It is usually found in a mountain. Hot magma, gas, and ash can escape through it.

props.alt: A volcano mountain with a crater

beats.narration: Magma is lighter than the rock around it. So it floats upward, like a bubble rising in a bath. It pushes up through cracks toward the top.
Magma also has tiny gas bubbles inside it. Think of a fizzy drink. When you open the bottle, the bubbles rush up and push the drink out!
As the magma rises, the squeezing gets weaker, and the bubbles grow bigger and bigger. They can grow thousands of times bigger! They shove the magma out, and the volcano erupts.

steps.label: Magma rises
steps.detail: It floats up from deep down

beats.narration: But not all volcanoes erupt the same way. Some go boom, and some just ooze. It all depends on how runny the magma is.

props.title: Boom or ooze?
props.subtitle: It depends on how runny the magma is

beats.narration: If the magma is thin and runny, the bubbles escape easily. The lava just flows out slowly, like syrup. Hawaii has volcanoes like this.

props.alt: slow lava flow at a volcano

beats.narration: If the magma is thick and sticky, the bubbles get stuck. Pressure builds and builds, then boom! It blasts out ash and rocks. Mount St. Helens did this in 1980.
Inside the volcano, we call it magma. Once it comes out, it gets a new name: lava! So now you know. Hot magma rises, bubbles push, and a volcano erupts!

props.text: Hot magma rises, bubbles push, and the volcano erupts!

accuracy.reason: Matches the notes: magma buoyancy, bubbles expanding thousands of times, runny vs sticky, St. Helens 1980. Small simplifications, such as 'like a bubble rising in a bath' and 'floats up', are fine for kids.

coverage.reason: Covers magma, the soda analogy, runny vs sticky, and magma vs lava. It lacks layers or a vent/crater explanation and a safe fun fact such as ash size, and it is probably short of 267 words.

structure.reason: Builds logically from magma to rising, bubbles, two eruption types, and a recap. Magma vs lava arrives late, in the last beat, and is tacked on.

hook_ending.reason: The hook 'the ground under your feet has a secret' is decent. The ending is a plain recap with no closing question or image.

tone.reason: Playful and simple, with short sentences and 'boom or ooze'. Some phrasing is slightly flat.

visuals.reason: Scene types vary well and match the narration (soda clip, steps, versus). The 'log-in' icon for 'Rises through cracks' is odd, and a definition card for a first term is fine.

originality.reason: The soda analogy and the syrup comparison are standard. The 'pinch of salt' gas fact from the notes is unused.
